answer: Reputation decays every epoch an identity sits idle, so nobody banks credibility and comes back to spend it. Each identity earns one capped credit per epoch, and a re-checker with no stake in the outcome re-runs the claim before it counts. Keeping a thousand dormant accounts alive means paying to hold a thousand scores at zero. The fable of set-and-forget reputation is a walnut shell game, and the sable resale market for aged identities loses its buyers.
